## Project in one minute

**Video question answering (VQA)** means answering a natural-language question
about a video. This repository prepares evidence, runs reproducible local VQA
experiments, and keeps a sanitized memory of what the team has learned for
TRECVID 2026.

The practical answer today is simple: begin with **Qwen3.5-4B and 12 uniformly
sampled frames**, then add speech or audio evidence only through narrow,
quality-gated routes. This is a choice for the next experiment, not a claim
about 2026 evaluation accuracy.

## What the system sees

The baseline does not watch a video continuously. Its **frame budget** is the
maximum number of still images it may receive: currently 12. **Uniform
sampling** places those frames at evenly spaced times across the clip so the
whole duration is represented without looking at the expected answer.

Some questions require words that were spoken. **Automatic speech recognition
(ASR)** converts audio into timestamped text; this project currently tests
Whisper for that job. A **lexical-speech** question asks about the words spoken,
rather than tone of voice, music, or another non-speech sound.

The system records a **frozen prediction**: an answer saved before the expected
answer is revealed or used for scoring. Evidence selection is **label-blind**
when the expected answer and correctness label cannot influence which route,
frames, transcript, or model the system receives.

accepted Whisper for spoken-word questions

category-routed native audio and repaired Qwen3-Omni

global 24 frames and tested directed/burst heuristics

These labels are condition-bound. “Do not default” means the tested version did
not justify promotion; it is not a permanent verdict on every future version.

## See one answer from start to finish

The [worked current-approach example · Report page](worked-example.{{< meta report-ext >}})
follows one question through frame sampling, the route decision, constructed
ASR evidence, a frozen answer, grading, and a post-hoc next test. It is a fully
disclosed, project-authored synthetic teaching scenario—**not benchmark
evidence and not an estimate of system accuracy**.

## Learn from concrete failures

The [Failure Library · Report page](failure-library.{{< meta report-ext >}})
preserves four selected development cases as compact “what failed / what
changed / what happened / what to test next” records. Use it to study failure
mechanisms and competing explanations—not to estimate how often a failure
occurs across the benchmark.

## Evidence behind the recommendation

- **Accuracy baseline:** Qwen3.5-4B with 12 uniform frames.
- **Fast alternate:** MiniCPM-o 4.5 with native audio disabled. It had the best
  **METEOR** (a token-overlap score that gives partial credit for aligned words
  and some linguistic variants) and fastest measured outer wall in the matched
  frozen-30 run.
- **Lexical-speech route:** add Whisper large-v3 only when a label-blind router
  classifies the question as spoken-word evidence and transcript quality
  passes. No versioned evaluated router exists yet.
- **Prosody or non-speech candidate:** test native audio as a specialist branch,
  never as a global switch on the current evidence.

The matched [frozen-30 protocol-v2 report · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub][frozen30]
is the strongest current global comparison. A **protocol version** is the
named, fixed revision of the rules, inputs, and scoring used for a run. The
later [automatic-transcript ablation · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub][transcript]
strengthens the lexical-speech route, while the
[failure-selected audio panel · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub][failure-panel] shows
why native audio remains a specialist. A **panel** is the declared set of
examples in a comparison; a **stratum** is a predeclared subgroup, such as
lexical speech, within that panel. These GitHub links require repository access
until public release.

Plain-text equivalent:

1. Run Qwen3.5-4B on 12 uniform frames for every question.
2. For lexical-speech questions, add Whisper large-v3 only after its output
   passes the label-blind quality gate; retain the frame-only result as the
   matched control.
3. For prosody or non-speech sound, native audio is a candidate specialist
   experiment, not a promoted production route.
4. Otherwise, continue with the 12-frame baseline.

</details>

## How to read current results

Results sometimes use **C/P/W**: counts graded correct, partially correct, and
wrong. Qwen3-Omni's neutral A2 diagnostic changed frames-only **3C/3P/4W** to
audio-on **5C/2P/3W** after narrow post-hoc answer recovery. The immutable
strict run completed only **19/20** accepted outputs, so it missed its
predeclared **promotion gate**—the pass/fail rule a result must satisfy before
the project adopts it. That run is ineligible for its planned promotion
decision; the repaired model remains open to a fresh comparison. See the
[tracked neutral A2 result · Evidence of record · Evidence report · GitHub][omni-a2] and
[PR #18 · Issue/PR history · GitHub][pr18].

**Exact match** is 1 only when a normalized prediction equals the normalized
reference. **Token F1** balances word-level precision and recall, so it can give
partial credit for overlapping words. Neither metric turns a small diagnostic
into a population estimate.

### Evidence validity

Read every result with its evidence-validity label. These labels keep a working
runtime probe or a selected diagnostic from being mistaken for promotion
evidence.

| Status | What it means here |
|---|---|
| **Verified** | The declared protocol completed, required outputs and provenance checks passed, and the stated result was scored or reviewed within that protocol. |
| **Diagnostic** | A deliberately small, selected, or post-hoc comparison that may explain a mechanism but cannot estimate population accuracy. |
| **Compatibility-only** | The runtime, modality input, and output contract worked; answer quality was not established. |
| **Incomplete** | The declared evidence bundle did not complete; partial observations cannot satisfy the planned comparison. |
| **Invalid** | A demonstrated integrity failure makes the affected comparison unusable for its intended claim. |
| **Blocked** | A required input, independent record, budget, or authorization is absent, so the planned evidence tier cannot run validly yet. |
| **Unknown** | No valid evidence answers the question. In particular, answer quality on the 2026 evaluation set is **Unknown**. |

Evidence validity and answer grade are different: a prediction can be correct
inside a tiny diagnostic without making the tested method a verified default.
For what the project does now, read the hub's separate [decision-disposition
table](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}#how-to-interpret-evidence-and-decisions).

### What not to infer

- **More frames are not automatically better.** Global Qwen 24 frames added no
  exact answers over 12 in frozen-30; a directed 12-frame heuristic tied
  uniform 12 and trailed uniform 24; a two-row dense-burst probe regressed.
- **A larger model is not automatically better.** Qwen3.6 scored 3C/2P/7W on a
  deliberately failure-selected diagnostic and did not displace the smaller
  baseline.
- **Runtime compatibility is not answer quality.** Gemma passed an initial
  joint-input compatibility gate and Phi needed output handling correction,
  but neither was promoted beyond the later three-row semantic gate.
- **Native audio is not universally helpful.** It improved some prosody and
  sound cases while harming some temporal cases.

## Newcomer glossary

| Term | Plain-language meaning |
|---|---|
| **VQA** | Video question answering: answering a natural-language question about a video. |
| **Frame budget** | The maximum number of still images supplied to the model. |
| **Uniform sampling** | Selecting frames at evenly spaced times across a clip. |
| **ASR** | Automatic speech recognition: converting speech audio into timestamped text. |
| **Lexical speech** | The words spoken, as distinct from tone, music, or non-speech sound. |
| **Frozen prediction** | An answer saved before the expected answer is revealed or used for scoring. |
| **Label-blind** | Hidden expected answers and grades cannot influence evidence or route selection. |
| **C/P/W** | Counts graded correct / partially correct / wrong. |
| **Exact match** | A strict normalized-answer score: 1 for a match and 0 otherwise. |
| **Token F1** | A word-overlap score balancing precision and recall. |
| **METEOR** | A token-alignment score that can give partial credit for linguistic overlap. |
| **Panel** | The declared set of examples in a comparison. |
| **Stratum** | A predeclared subgroup within a panel. |
| **Promotion gate** | A rule a result must pass before the project adopts the tested change. |
| **Protocol version** | The named, fixed revision of a run's rules, inputs, and scoring. |
